rods.name: Bamboo Rod
rods.description: A simple bamboo pole. Gets the job done.

rods.name: Driftwood Staff
rods.description: Heavy and slow, but the wide tip gives you a more forgiving catch window.

rods.name: Fiberglass Rod
rods.description: Lighter than bamboo with a wider tip. Gives you a more forgiving catch window.

rods.name: Reef Guard
rods.description: Responsive and fast. Bites come a little quicker than the baseline.

rods.name: Telescoping Rod
rods.description: Extends deep. Something about the length draws rarer fish to the surface.

rods.name: Moonwood Staff
rods.description: Carved from driftwood blessed by a full moon. Quicker bites and a wider catch window.

rods.name: Graphite Rod
rods.description: Lightweight and stiff. Noticeably quicker bites.

rods.name: Navigator's Rod
rods.description: A well-balanced deep-sea rod. Good speed and a wider catch zone.

rods.name: Carbon Rod
rods.description: Precision-engineered for quick, snappy bites.

rods.name: Deep Diver
rods.description: Built for the abyss. Fast bites and a wide catch window.

rods.name: Legendary Rod
rods.description: Forged from the mast of a sunken galleon. Faster bites, and the rarest fish cannot resist.

rods.name: Twin-Strike
rods.description: Two hooks on one line. When luck strikes, they both bite.

rods.name: Second Wind
rods.description: Stubborn rod. When you miss, sometimes it refuses to let go.

rods.name: Millionaire's Rod
rods.description: Hand-rolled in gold leaf. Every catch brings two.

rods.name: YOLO Rod
rods.description: Roll the dice every cast for a 100-fish haul — and the odds climb the shallower you fish. The rest of the time? Just a regular catch.

rods.name: Completionist Rod
rods.description: Forged from the soul of every species in the sea. A master's tool on its own, and a vessel besides: fit up to three rods you own into it to carry their gifts, and re-forge whenever you like.

rods.name: Treasure Rod
rods.description: Lures the deep’s lost hoards — doubles your chance of hooking a crate.

rods.name: Perfect Rod
rods.description: Rewards flawless form — perfect catches grant double XP, and it scales with your streak.

rods.name: Galaxy Rod
rods.description: Spun from cosmic thread. After any catch, open a wormhole and reroll it into a different fish from the same waters — fortune or folly, you take what surfaces.

rods.name: Lightsaber Rod
rods.description: A blade of pure energy. Fish are drawn to the light — most casts bite almost the instant your line touches the water.

rods.name: Yoon's Locked-In Rod
rods.description: Rewards a hot hand. Chain perfect catches to LOCK IN: 3 in a row quickens your bites, 5 lands a triple haul on every catch, and 10 quickens them further into a rare-fish frenzy. Hold the streak to keep it all — one miss and you start over.

baits.name: Worms
baits.description: Reliable all-purpose bait. Claim 20 free from your Daily Bonus.

baits.name: Night Crawler
baits.description: Fish bite 15% faster. Widens your catch zone by 4° — a bigger catch zone means more room to land the needle.

baits.name: Angler's Formula
baits.description: Fish bite 35% faster. Widens your catch zone by 8° — a bigger catch zone means more room to land the needle.

baits.name: Luminous Lure
baits.description: Fish bite 40% faster and the catch zone widens by 10°. Earned from expeditions and bounties, or bought with Fathoms in the Locker. Something ancient stirs when it glows.
baits.hint: Something ancient stirs when it glows.

baits.name: Golden Lure
baits.description: Fish bite 45% faster. Widens your catch zone by 10°. The finest lure in existence — a rare drop, or bought with Fathoms in the Locker. The oldest things in the deep rise for its shine.
baits.hint: The oldest things in the deep rise for its shine.

lines.name: Copolymer
lines.description: Blended nylon. More give, less break.

lines.name: Titanium Wire
lines.description: Near-zero stretch. Cuts through current like nothing.

lines.name: Deep Sea Line
lines.description: Built for the abyss. Almost nothing breaks it.

reels.name: Precision Reel

reels.name: Tournament Reel

reels.name: Deep Sea Reel
reels.description: Engineered for the deep. The needle barely hurries.

reels.name: Kraken's Grip
reels.description: Forged to hold something ancient. The needle drifts, almost lazy.

reels.name: Tidecaller's Reel

hooks.name: Copper Hook

hooks.name: Bronze Hook
hooks.description: Forged bronze. A touch sturdier than copper.

hooks.name: Iron Hook
hooks.description: Solid iron. A noticeably wider catch window.

hooks.name: Steel Hook
hooks.description: Tempered steel. Reliable in any depth.

hooks.name: Silver Hook
hooks.description: Polished silver. Catches the light — and the fish.

hooks.name: Gold Hook
hooks.description: Polished gold. Fish can't resist the shine.

hooks.name: Enchanted Hook
hooks.description: Glows faintly. Something stirs in the deep.

hooks.name: Abyssal Hook
hooks.description: Drawn from the dark. The catch window is remarkably wide.

hooks.name: Legendary Hook
hooks.description: Said to have been lost at sea — and returned.

shinyMessages: A golden {fish}. The kind of catch sailors carve into the hull.
{fish} of gold under your hand. Captain, this is one in a thousand.
Sailors tell tales of gold-scaled ones. Tonight you've held one.
A gilded {fish} — the sea's own coin. Mount it, or part with it for a king's haul.
Gold-scaled and impossible. Even the old captains only saw one of these.
A {fish} drawn up in solid gold. The dockside won't believe you without proof.
Worth more than a hold of common haul, and rarer than the stories about it.
The crew has gone quiet. None of them have ever seen a golden one before.
A golden {fish}. Every captain hopes for this once in a career.
The deep turned a {fish} to gold tonight, and gave it to you.

lines.text: ...*Megalodon.*
The last one. The one all the others were only ever leading up to.
All six. In a single pair of hands.
Do you have any notion what you have just finished building?
Years I stood at that black water, and it would not open for me. Not one inch. And you...
You were exactly what it was waiting for. Exactly what *I* was waiting for.
Never mind. Old rivals get sentimental.
Go on. Enjoy your wall of monsters.
The long-neck. *Plesiosaurus.* I have watched that thing take a rig and swim off like it felt nothing.
It let you land it. Sat in your hands like it decided to.
The deep does not just decide. Not for most of us.
Hm. Go on, then.
*Dunkleosteus.* A jaw like a ship's prow, older than the first keel that ever cut this water.
I hooked it once. It took my line and left me the story. That is all it has ever left anyone.
It handed you the whole fish. I would sit a while with why.
...or do not. Just keep pulling them up.
*Mosasaurus.* The sea-dragon every old chart drew a hard border around.
Turns out that border was the only honest ink on the page.
Every soul who chased these is a name cut in stone now. Every one but you.
That was never luck. Luck drowned a long way back. You are something the water wants.
The *Basilosaurus.* It swam this water before there was a single soul alive to fear it.
I have wanted to look one of these in the eye my whole life. Never once got the chance.
And here it lies on your deck, dripping like a market cod.
Sits wrong, does it not. ...Good. It ought to.
*Shastasaurus.* The largest thing that ever drew breath in salt water, and it is on your hook.
The others all swore these were stories. Easier than admitting they were out of reach.
They were never out of yours. The deep keeps handing you what it kept from me.
...from everyone. So keep pulling, captain. I mean to see just how far those hands of yours can reach.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: A weathered ship slides out of the fog. Barnacle-crusted hull, patched sails, and cannons aimed at your ship already.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: So another pup thinks they can take old Barnie. Many have tried... none've sailed home.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: I've been raiding these waters longer than you've been alive. Don't matter. You'll be back where you started before long.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Don't let Pete scare you. He's all bark... or whatever sound it is that he makes.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: He's cocky only because he's never had a real challenge before.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: What're ya waiting for, lil pup? Got cold fins now that you've seen me in the flesh?

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: You love hearing yourself talk don't ya, Pete. Let's take him down cap'n. Can't stand to hear him talk anymore.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Ready your guns. This is where your story ends.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: So you're the little hook that's been snagging my freight. Wondered why my couriers've been late.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Captain Krusty was it? I see why you got that name.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Don't you dare disrespect me. I own these straits. You lot are meddling in business where you don't belong.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: You may run these straits, but I run these streets.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: That didn't come out as hard as you'd think, Mako.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Regrets.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: Krust looks annoyed. But you weren't trying to be friends anyway.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: You've cost me enough time. It's time to pay up.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Someone above you. There is always someone above. This whole sea is just fish too frightened to look up, captain. Let us give this one a reason to.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Strike your colors or strike your guns. Either way this consignment sails on without you.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: The fog thickens until sea and sky blur into dull gray. Out of it, a slow-built ship glides up. Decks stacked with rolled charts and brass-bound sextants.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: I heard a young captain was reading my routes.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: It's him. The Finndicate's chartmaker.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: I prefer to be called The Cartographer. Has a nicer ring to it. You cut off my supply line from Krust. It's unfortunate, he was easy to work with. If a bit naive.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: No matter. The charts are nearly complete. I won't have time to entertain you any longer.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Entertain us? We were just about to show YOU a good time.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Me? You won't even be able to reach me. That's us chartmakers... always playing the background.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Why are you working for the Finndicate at all?

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Mm... we've got bigger goals than the tiny brains of yours can even comprehend. Now if you'll excuse me.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: We're not letting him get away. Let's show him that pen and paper can't do what a cannon can.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: You sailed into the Gullet and brought down ranks of low barracuda hulls to arrive at the Tollmaster himself.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: You've come a long way down my channel, captain. I see that you've become a bit too familiar with the finances of the Finndicate. That's my sea to sail. Not yours.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Tollmaster Spet... I presume. Why do all the operations go through you? What's the purpose of the Gullet?

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: I handle the Finndicate's accounting. Sounds boring, but it gives me a ton of power. And control. You've messed with our bottom line by sinking some of our best. And that's not something that we just write off.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: The Finndicate doesn't just do normal business anymore, it seems. What are you guys really up to?

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: You've got captains feeding you stolen resources. A cartographer supplying you charts to... who knows where. None of this makes sense... at least in any good way.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Who determines what's good? I just make sure everything balances out.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Then surely you know that there's some illegal activity going on within the Finndicate!

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: No one audits me. I say what's illegal or not. And the only thing I know that is illegal is your trespassing into my territory.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: I've never met an accountant that could fight.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: You're a fool then. Our battles are done with numbers.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Let's show Spet who's putting up the real numbers.

phase2.dialogueLine: Enough games. Run out the real guns.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: Past the harbor wall the Coffers open up: a drowned market ringed by guns, and a line of Galleons already coming about to meet you.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Far enough, captain. Nobody sails into the Coffers uninvited and lives to count the take.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: You're a long way from the docks for a harbormaster.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Admiral, to you. I keep this wall, and my gunners fly whatever colors the market needs. You'll never know which gun is the live one until it's already in you.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: A fleet that lies about which gun is loaded. How quaint. I have already told the captain which of yours are bluffing, admiral. Do keep pretending.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Run out your guns. *Mine are already lying to you.*

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Everything in this drowned market lies. I came back from its floor to say so, admiral. Your painted colors do not frighten a dead man.

phases.dialogueLine: You cracked the ledger. You have not cleared the debt.

check.name: The Big Gun
check.telegraph: The Quartermaster hauls the reserve cannon onto the rail and swings the muzzle toward you.
check.hint: A shot this heavy has to be met with a crew ability. A defensive one that gets something between you and the muzzle before it fires. Your own brace/dodge won’t turn it aside.
check.counteredLine: The big shot slams into your cover and glances wide.
check.failLine: The reserve cannon speaks, and nothing turned it aside.

phases.dialogueLine: You think the shelves are bare? I keep a reserve deck for captains like you.

check.name: Cooking the Books
check.telegraph: The Quartermaster ducks low behind the counter and starts working the ledger, fast.
check.hint: Don't let him finish the tally. Fire a crew ability to break it. Something disrupting to foul his concentration, or a heavy-hitting one to overpower him before the count closes, or he balances the ledger in his favor.
check.counteredLine: You break his tally before it can close.
check.failLine: The ledger balances in his favor.

phases.dialogueLine: Nothing left to sell. Then I sink you and take the lot back myself.

check.name: Fire Sale
check.telegraph: The Quartermaster touches a torch to the stock and the whole Cache goes up in flame.
check.hint: The whole stock goes up at once and sets your hull ablaze. Fire a crew ability before it catches, a recovery one or a defensive one, and if it does catch, only a crew heal puts the fire out.
check.counteredLine: You smother the blaze before it can spread.
check.failLine: The fire sale catches, and your hull goes up in flame.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: The Cache's shutters roll up into a gun-deck, and the keeper stands behind a counter of run-out cannon, smiling like he's already counted your coin.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Every captain who ever beat me bought the means to do it off my own shelf. *You included.*

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Then I will beat you with the one thing I never bought off your shelf, keeper. My teeth.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Then we'll sink you with your own goods. Hold still.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Your goods? Everything you carry was a loan, captain. *And I am calling one back.*

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Let's see how bold you sail once I reach across the counter and take back the piece you leaned on most.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Take your trinkets back, keeper. The one thing you never sold this captain is the crew standing on her deck. Good luck reaching across the counter for us.

phases.dialogueLine: Sink me? Lad, I have been at the bottom for years. Try taking something off me instead.

check.name: The Salvage
check.telegraph: He swings a crane over the rail and hauls up the reinforced plating you never came back for. He means to wear it.
check.hint: Disrupt him. He cannot bolt it on if he cannot work.
check.counteredLine: The crane fouls and the plating goes back over the side. He does not take that well.
check.failLine: He bolts your plating over his own ribs and the holes close up.

phases.dialogueLine: You left the fire-shot on my counter. I have had a long time to think about where to put it.

check.name: The Long Burn
check.telegraph: He packs the incendiary you passed over and stands there holding a lit match, in no hurry at all.
check.hint: Survive it. Get a barrier up, or be ready to put the fire out.
check.counteredLine: The shot bursts against the barrier and burns itself out on open water.
check.failLine: Your own fire-shot goes through the deck and the ship starts to cook.

phases.dialogueLine: Every captain I ever armed, I watched sink. I always did keep the good glass back.

check.name: The Called Shot
check.telegraph: He raises your Gunner's Sight to a dead eye, takes the bearing off your own compass, and holds it. He does not need to hurry.
check.hint: Defend. Put something between you and a shot that is already aimed.
check.counteredLine: The shot lands where your hull was and finds a braced wall instead. He mutters something about waste.
check.failLine: He fires down your own sights. The shot goes exactly where he meant it to.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: The gun-deck is exactly as you left it, down to the lantern oil. The counter is still stocked. The keeper is still behind it, and you can see the shutters through him.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Dead men keep better books than living ones. Everything you left on my counter, everything you melted down since. I have it all, and I have *all the time there is*.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Then you'll not mind us taking it back off you. Twice, if it comes to that.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: *They always come back.* That is the one thing I could ever count on.

special.name: Dig In
special.line: The Bank drops his weight into the silt and settles, and the shot just thumps into mud.

special.name: Deadwood
special.line: Root and deadwood come up under the hull and wrap the rudder, and the wheel goes dead in your hands.

special.name: Chain-Shot
special.line: Chain-shot screams through your powder line and your guns cough where they roared.

special.name: Hull-Cracker
special.line: A cracker round splits your seams wide open, and every blow after it will find the gap.

special.name: Old Wounds
special.line: Old Scar takes the hit the way he has taken every other one, and the hole closes while you watch.

special.name: Gag Order
special.line: The gag order comes down, and your crew go quiet mid-shout.

special.name: Still Water
special.line: Sal stops moving. The chop goes flat around him, and every gun on the line goes quiet.

phases.dialogueLine: The don said bring him your colors. He never said in one piece.

check.name: The Death Roll
check.telegraph: Sal takes your hull in his teeth, sets his feet against the swell, and starts to turn.
check.hint: He is going to roll, and he will not let go. Only a crew ability gets something between your hull and that grip. Your own brace or dodge does nothing here.
check.counteredLine: He rolls against braced timber, tears off a mouthful of nothing, and lets go spitting splinters.
check.failLine: He rolls, and he keeps rolling, and your hull comes apart along the grain.

phases.dialogueLine: You want the don? Then come through my back. Nothing you carry goes through my back. Not one shot of it.

preFightDialogue.speaker: narrator
preFightDialogue.text: The blockade line rides the swell ahead: the don's own escort armada, lanterns doused, gunports open. At the center of it, something long and low sits *so still in the water you take it for a spar*.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: Far enough, captain. The don's water starts where your charts stop.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Then we're exactly where we mean to be. Move your line.

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: Move it, or be moved with it. I have shifted reefs that argued less than you, enforcer.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: The Quartermaster talked too much and kept too little. I do not talk, and *I do not let go*. Ask anyone who ever got this far.

preFightDialogue.speaker: boss
preFightDialogue.text: You will not see me move. *You will only notice I have you.*

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew
preFightDialogue.text: I noticed you an hour ago, love. A thing that lies that still is a thing afraid to move first. Let us find out what it is afraid of.

ultimate.name: Broadside Royale
ultimate.line: Every gun on the deck speaks at once, in the don’s name.

special.name: False Court
special.line: Lantern-rigs bloom down his rail, a court of false colors with only one throne among them.

special.name: Iron Etiquette
special.line: Iron shutters slam over every line you’d take. Nobody reaches the don in one knock.

special.name: Kingmaker’s Gale
special.line: He whistles a wind out of dead water, and your gun-deck pitches with it.

special.name: Omertà
special.line: The left hand draws a line across his throat, and your crew’s shouts die in the wind.

ultimate.name: The Quiet Word
ultimate.line: What the don whispers, the guns repeat.

special.name: Marked for the Don
special.line: He reads your name off a short list, and every gun in the court knows where to aim.

ultimate.name: Final Counsel
ultimate.line: His advice, delivered all at once.

phase2.dialogueLine: You do not close an account by sinking it once, captain. Let me show you the interest.

special.name: Court of Crowns
special.line: The court closes around the throne. A dozen crowns, and only one that bleeds.

ultimate.name: The Deep Verdict
ultimate.line: The don passes sentence, and the water carries it out.

openingCheck.name: The Don’s Court
openingCheck.telegraph: The whole drowned court trains its guns on your hull at once, waiting on the don’s nod.
openingCheck.hint: You cannot out-gun a whole court. Weather the opening volley. A brace, a shield, or a big heal will all ride it out.
openingCheck.counteredLine: Your crew answers first, and the court’s opening volley scatters wide.
openingCheck.failLine: Nobody stands with you, and the whole court fires as one.

phases.dialogueLine: You came for a don. The deep sent you something older. Look at the WIDTH of what you’ve been bargaining with.

check.name: The Maw
check.telegraph: The don’s hull ROLLS, and keeps rolling, a jaw the size of your broadside opening under the waterline.
check.hint: A bite that wide can’t be weaved. Harden the hull with a brace, or blast the jaw apart with a big shot before it shuts.
check.counteredLine: Your crew throws the maw off its line and it grinds iron instead of deck.
check.failLine: The maw closes on your hull and something structural gives. Every blow after this one finds the gap.

phases.dialogueLine: There it is. The blood. Now the whole ocean knows where you are.

check.name: Blood in the Water
check.telegraph: He rakes a long gash down your hull and circles wide, the sea reddening with every pass at the smell of it.
check.hint: The wound is what keeps drawing him. Close it with a heal, or snare him off the blood-trail before he circles back in.
check.counteredLine: Your crew answers the wound and the blood-trail goes cold; he loses the scent.
check.failLine: He follows the blood straight in, tears the gash wider, and the wound feeds him.

phases.dialogueLine: Enough court. Enough colors. The Finndicate was never the family, captain. It was the FEEDING.

check.name: The Sounding
check.telegraph: The megalodon SOUNDS. The whole sea dips as he goes deep, gathering water for a breach that will land on your deck.
check.hint: You can’t block a falling mountain. You have to break the dive itself. Snare him out of it, or blast him up early with a big shot.
check.counteredLine: The dive breaks. He breaches early, wide, and the wave takes the blow for you.

preFightDialogue.text: We found it, don. The account your whole empire was really paying into. You were never the top of this, and you know it. Does that frighten you as much as it frightens your books?

preFightDialogue.speaker: crew

lines.text: Easy, now. Reel it in slow.
I've been watching that line of yours the better part of an hour. A line never lies about the hand on the far end of it.
Finn. There's not a current on this whole coast I haven't read, and I've watched a hundred anglers strut down this dock and wash back up it empty.
Yours sits different in the water. *Promise*, some would call it. Cheap word.
Let's see what the deep makes of you.
Back already.
Didn't take you for the stubborn kind. Good. The water eats the other kind alive.
Quick hands. I'll grant you that much, and not one word more.
There's water past the edge of every chart you own. *Old* water.
The fish down there would take your finest trophy for a minnow and swim off still hungry.
Most anglers swear it isn't real. Easier than admitting it's simply out of their reach.
Take the bet. Let's find out if it's out of yours.
The Ancient Deep.
Past your trench, past your abyss, where the water turns to ink and the seafloor forgets to stop falling.
Six things worth the pulling live down there. Six. Not five. Not seven.
Funny, the numbers a captain finds himself counting in the dark.
I've stood at the lip of that deep more nights than I would ever admit to you.
Dropped a line straight down into the black. Every time, nothing. Like the water just hands it back up, polite as you please.
Some doors only open for the right grip.
Mine has never once been it.
A hundred anglers I've watched come down this dock. You're the hundred and first.
The rest were all noise. You're quieter. Steadier.
The water doesn't seem to mind you. I've learned to pay mind when it doesn't.
Hooked something down there, once. Held it a full thirty seconds.
Then the line went slack. Slow. Gentle. Like the deep was handing it back on *purpose*.
Like it knew whose hands were on the rod, and decided no.
All six trophies. Landed by a single pair of hands.
You've any notion what that's worth? What a thing like that would *open*?
...course you don't. Keep fishing. You will.
Some waters take more than they ever give back.
The Ancient Deep takes *everything*. Everything but the worthy.
So be worthy. And be quick about it. I've done enough waiting for one lifetime.
Long enough at this trade, you quit hooking. You start *listening*.
The water tells you what's coming up the line. Tells you exactly what it is, if you shut your mouth and let it.
Have you touched the Ancient Deep yet? Truly touched it. Not paddled the shallows of it.
...no. You haven't.
I'd know. I always know. Take the bet, then. Off with you.
There's a steadiness in you, under all that mess. That's the rare part.
That's the part I've been looking f...
...the part worth *beating*. Forget I said it. Cast.
You're the closest anyone has ever come. Closer than you would believe.
Pull up all six, and we'll both finally see what they're good for.
Slip of an old tongue. Cast your line.
Hmph. Beginner's luck.
Don't go framing it.
Twice now. *Twice.*
...all right. The water didn't hand you that. You took it. Try not to waste a thing you're willing to take.
Five times. Maybe you're not completely useless after all.
Don't let it swell your head. There's a whole ocean left, and most of it's meaner than me.
You're getting faster. I've noticed.
I notice everything. It's cost me more sleep than I'd care to say.
Most folk can't take me twice. You've done it eight.
Patience, and a steady hand. That's the whole trade, start to finish.
Took me half a lifetime to learn it.
You're picking it up fast. Almost *unfairly* fast.
Where'd you learn to read water like that? You don't move like some inland kid who wandered down to the docks.
...no. Don't answer.
I'd rather wonder.
Where do *I* come from? Ha.
Nowhere you'll find inked on any chart you own.
And we'll be keeping it that way.
Two anglers walk into a tavern. One of them catches a fish. The other one's me.
...you laughed.
Good. I was starting to worry about you.
Patient on the entry. *Mean* on the pull. That's how a body fishes the deep, if the deep allows it.
And I'm starting to think it just might allow *you*.
I gave that deep ten years. Ten years of cold mornings, a slack line, and silence.
You might wring more out of it in a single season than I got from every one of them.
The deep has taken things off me I don't put into words.
Leave it where it lies. Take the work, or don't.
That look you get, locking onto a perfect. Like the water slows itself down just for you.
I've only ever seen it on the kind of angler who can go where I can't.
Thirty jobs. Most anglers don't last thirty *casts*.
...I won't call you my equal. But I'll quit calling you 'kid.'
Spend that sparingly. I don't hand it out twice.
Trick to the deep zones: don't pull at the bite. Pull at the *breath* right after it.
A fish has to recover. Hit it in the recovery and it can't run.
...not that I told you anything.
All these years working this dock. Waiting for the right line to come walking up it.
Didn't quite believe it ever truly would.
Forty. You've taken everything I can teach you from up here on the dock.
The rest, only the deep can teach. So go down and take it.
...for the both of us.
...you did it.
First trophy up out of the Ancient Deep. In one piece. You actually *did* it.
Listen to me. Whatever you think you're holding, you're holding less than half of it.
There are five more down there. Five. And I need every last one of them landed.
...*need*.
Poor word, for a rival. Let's call it *want* and leave it there.
I have spent more of my life on that black water than I will ever tell you. Not once did it open for me. Not once.
It's opening for you.
So here's the new bet. The only one that ever mattered. You and me. All six.
I didn't come to this dock to fish, if you must know. I came to find someone who *could*.
Took longer than I'd have liked. Don't ask me why. Just fish.

epilogueIdle: Back at it. How many of the six now?
...you've been down to the deep again. I can see it on you.
How's the black water treating you?
Don't let the rest of this ocean distract you. Six. That's the only number that counts.
epilogueLore: I've burned more rigs on that deep than you've owned in your life. Never kept a single bite.
The deep knows who it'll allow down. I'm not on its list. You might be.
Six trophies in one hand. You've no notion what that unlocks. You will.

asks.they: Finn. I fish, I watch, and I am here more than anybody sensible would be.
Because you are new and I am not, and one of us is going to be interesting to the other.

asks.you: What is worth catching out here?
asks.they: Everything, until you have caught it. Then almost nothing. That is the trouble with the shallows.

asks.you: How long have you been out here?
asks.they: Longer than the harbor has had a name I recognize. I stopped counting on purpose.
Every day. Do not ask me what I catch.

asks.you: What is the furthest you have been?
asks.they: The lip of the old water. Never over it. Never once over it.

asks.you: What is actually down in the Ancient Deep?
asks.they: Six things worth the pulling. I have said that before and I will keep saying it until somebody proves me wrong or right.

asks.you: Why does it matter that it is six?
asks.they: Because six is a set. Five is a collection and seven is a mess. Six is a thing somebody could finish.

asks.you: What happens if somebody lands all six?
asks.they: ...ask me that one again when it is not hypothetical.

asks.you: You said your line comes back empty. Every time?
asks.they: Every time. Forty years of every time. You get used to the sound of nothing on the other end.

asks.you: Do you resent me for it?
asks.they: Some days. Not most. It turns out watching it happen is closer than never seeing it at all.
Because a hand like yours goes soft if nobody asks anything of it. And because I want to see how far it goes.

asks.you: Why are you really out here?
asks.they: I came looking for somebody who could do the thing I cannot. I have been looking a very long time.
Now I have found them and I am not entirely sure what I am supposed to feel about it.

asks.you: What do you want from all six?
asks.they: To see it. That is what I will tell you today, and it is not the whole of it, and you already knew that.

quests.label: Land 8 fish in the Shallows
quests.give: Nothing clever. Go and pull eight out of the water and come back to me. I want to watch how you hold the rod, not what you catch with it.
quests.done: Eight. And not one of them fought you the same way twice. I noticed.
quests.waiting: Eight. You are not at eight. Off you go.
quests.gated: Go and fish. Come back when you have done some of it.

quests.label: Land 4 perfect catches in the Shallows
quests.give: Anybody can land a fish. Land four PERFECT and I will start paying attention properly.
quests.done: Four clean ones. Most anglers manage that by accident once a season.
quests.waiting: Four perfect. Not four fish. There is a difference and it is the entire difference.
quests.gated: Not yet. Get some water under you first.

quests.label: Land 15 fish in the Shallows
quests.give: Fifteen out of the shallow water. It is not hard and it is not meant to be. It is meant to be a habit.
quests.done: Fifteen. You have stopped thinking about the shallows, which means they are finished with you.
quests.waiting: The Shallows. Fifteen. You have been elsewhere, have you not.
quests.gated: Start where everybody starts.

quests.label: Land 2 uncommon or better in the Shallows
quests.give: Two that are not the usual. The shallow water has better in it than people think, they just stop looking.
quests.done: Two. You have started seeing what is actually down there rather than what you expected.
quests.waiting: Uncommon or better. Look properly.
quests.gated: Go and fish first.

quests.label: Land 3 perfect catches in a row in the Shallows
quests.give: Three without a miss. It is the smallest run worth calling a run, and you will be surprised how it goes wrong.
quests.done: Three straight. Do that ten more times and it stops being luck.
quests.waiting: In a row. One miss and it starts again.
quests.gated: Not yet.

quests.label: Land 30 fish in the Shallows
quests.give: Thirty. Any water, any fish. There is no trick to this one, I want the hours in your hands.
quests.done: Thirty. That is the part nobody puts in the stories and it is most of the work.
quests.waiting: Thirty. You are not close and that is fine.
quests.gated: Go and fish.

quests.label: Land 10 fish in Open Waters
quests.give: The Shallows have taught you everything they are going to. Take ten out of Open Waters and stop wading.
quests.done: Ten, out where the bottom stops being a suggestion. Good.
quests.waiting: Open Waters. Past the shelf. You have not been out there enough.
quests.gated: Open Waters is the next thing and you are not rated for it yet. Go and get levelled.

quests.label: Land 5 perfect catches in a row in Open Waters
quests.give: Five in a row. Not five in a day, five without a single miss between them. That is a hand, not a habit.
quests.done: Five straight. I have watched a hundred anglers try that and I am not exaggerating the number.
quests.waiting: In a ROW. One miss and you start again. That is what makes it worth asking for.
quests.gated: Come back when you have grown into it.

quests.label: Land 3 rare or better in Open Waters
quests.give: Three rare ones. The water decides who gets those, and I want to see whether it has decided about you.
quests.done: Three. The water is making up its mind about you, and I do not think it is going the way I expected.
quests.waiting: Rare, I said. Common fish are just weather.
quests.gated: Not at your level. The water does not hand those to beginners.

quests.label: Land 10 perfect catches in Open Waters
quests.give: Ten clean. Not in a row, just ten. I want to see whether the good ones are becoming the normal ones.
quests.done: Ten. They are becoming the normal ones.
quests.waiting: Ten perfect. Take as long as you like.
quests.gated: Come back when you are rated for this water.

quests.label: Land 25 fish in Open Waters
quests.give: Twenty five out of the middle water. Long job. Do it around everything else you are doing.
quests.done: Twenty five. You know that water now, which is different from having been there.
quests.waiting: Open Waters. Twenty five. It adds up faster than you think.
quests.gated: Not until you can work it.

quests.label: Land 60 fish in Open Waters
quests.give: Sixty, anywhere. I am not testing your nerve with this one, I am testing whether you keep going.
quests.done: Sixty. Most captains stop somewhere in the forties and never notice they stopped.
quests.waiting: Sixty. Keep at it.
quests.gated: Later.

quests.label: Land 12 fish in the Deep
quests.give: The Deep. Twelve of them. It is a long sail and that is deliberate, I want to see if you come back.
quests.done: Twelve, and you came back up. That second part is the one I was watching.
quests.waiting: The Deep. Past the abyss talk, before the black. Twelve.
quests.gated: The Deep is the next water and it is not open to you yet. Go and earn it.

quests.label: Land 20 perfect catches in the Deep
quests.give: Twenty perfect. Take your time. I am not going anywhere and neither, apparently, are you.
quests.done: Twenty. You have stopped counting them, have you not. That is when it starts working.
quests.waiting: Twenty clean. You are not there yet and there is no hurry.
quests.gated: Later. You are not deep enough into this.

quests.label: Land 8 perfect catches in a row in the Deep
quests.give: Eight in a row. I could not do six on my best day and I have had a great many days.
quests.done: Eight straight. I want to be sour about that and I find I am not.
quests.waiting: Eight, unbroken. It is meant to be hard. That is the whole of the request.
quests.gated: Not yet. Ask me again when the deep water knows your name.

quests.label: Land 4 rare or better in the Deep
quests.give: Four rare, out of deep water. They are down there in numbers the shallows never see.
quests.done: Four. The deep gives them up more readily to somebody it has decided about.
quests.waiting: Rare or better. Four of them.
quests.gated: The Deep first.

quests.label: Land 25 fish in the Deep
quests.give: Twenty five out of the Deep. That is a lot of sailing and I am aware of it.
quests.done: Twenty five. You have spent more hours down there this month than I have this year.
quests.waiting: The Deep. Twenty five. It is a long one on purpose.
quests.gated: Not yet.

quests.label: Land 100 fish in the Deep
quests.give: A hundred. Anywhere, anything. Nobody has ever asked you for a number like that and meant it kindly.
quests.done: A hundred. There is nothing clever about it and it is still the hardest thing I have asked you for.
quests.waiting: A hundred. Chip at it.
quests.gated: Later.

quests.label: Land 10 fish in the Abyss
quests.give: The Abyss. Ten. Everything down there has teeth or lights or both, and none of it has ever been polite to me.
quests.done: Ten out of the black. You did that in the time it takes most captains to work up to looking at it.
quests.waiting: The Abyss. Where it stops being blue. Ten of them.
quests.gated: The black water. Not at your level, and I am not sending you down there to prove me wrong.

quests.label: Land 5 epic or better in the Abyss
quests.give: Five of the real ones. Not rare. The ones the water only hands over when it has decided something about the hand on the rod.
quests.done: Five. It has decided, then.
quests.waiting: Epic or better. If you are not sure whether it counted, it did not.
quests.gated: Those do not come to captains at your level. Go on.

quests.label: Land 12 perfect catches in a row in the Abyss
quests.give: Twelve without a miss. There is nothing left I can ask you for that is harder than this and still fair.
quests.done: Twelve. Straight. I have run out of things to test and I am not sure what I do now.
quests.waiting: Twelve in a row. Take a season over it if you need to. I have waited longer.
quests.gated: Not yet. That one is for somebody further along than you.

quests.label: Land 40 perfect catches in the Abyss
quests.give: Forty clean ones. At this point I am not testing anything. I just want to watch you do it forty times.
quests.done: Forty. I have stopped being able to tell when you are trying.
quests.waiting: Forty perfect. No hurry on this one at all.
quests.gated: Not at your level.

quests.label: Land 22 fish in the Abyss
quests.give: Twenty two out of the black. Most captains never manage two. Take your lantern and your patience.
quests.done: Twenty two. You go down there the way other people go to the market.
quests.waiting: The Abyss. Twenty two of them.
quests.gated: The black water is not open to you.

quests.label: Land 2 legendary fish in the Abyss
quests.give: Two legendaries, before we go anywhere near the old water. I need to know you can do it on demand.
quests.done: Two. On demand. That is the last thing I needed to know and I already knew it.
quests.waiting: Legendary. Two of them. The water decides, but it decides about you differently now.
quests.gated: Not yet.

quests.label: Land 8 fish in the Ancient Deep
quests.give: The old water. Eight ordinary fish out of it, to start. I have told you what is down there and I have told you my line comes back empty. Yours will not.
quests.done: Eight out of the Ancient Deep. Do you understand that I have never held one of those? Not one.
quests.waiting: The oldest water on your chart. Eight. I would go with you if it would do any good.
quests.gated: The old water is not open to you yet. I have waited forty years. I can wait for you.

quests.label: Land 3 legendary fish in the Ancient Deep
quests.give: Three legendaries. Not because I doubt you. Because I want to watch it happen and this is the only way I get to.
quests.done: Three. You make the impossible look like a Tuesday, and I have stopped pretending that does not sting.
quests.waiting: Legendary. The water gives those to almost nobody. It will give them to you.
quests.gated: Not yet. Those are the far end of it.

quests.label: Raise the Plesiosaurus
quests.give: The first of the six. A long neck and a longer memory, and it comes up slow, like it is deciding about you. And you will not manage it on worms, so listen. They rise for a shine: a Golden Lure will raise one, a Luminous will do it slower, and nothing else on your boat will do it at all. Forty years I stood at the lip of that water with the wrong thing on my line.
quests.done: You are holding one. An actual one of the six. I am going to need a moment and I would rather you did not watch.
quests.waiting: The Plesiosaurus. Golden Lure, old water, and patience. It is down there.
quests.gated: Not until the old water opens to you.

quests.label: Raise the Dunkleosteus
quests.give: Second. This one is armor plate and a bite that never needed teeth. Same lure, same water. It will not come up politely.
quests.done: Two. You have landed two of them and I have landed none, and I find I am not as sour about that as I expected to be.
quests.waiting: The Dunkleosteus. Keep the shine on your line.
quests.gated: Not yet.

quests.label: Raise the Mosasaurus
quests.give: Third. The one that hunts the dark on purpose rather than living in it. Do not fight it early, it is stronger at the start than it is at the end.
quests.done: Three. Half the set. Nobody in the history of this harbor has been halfway.
quests.waiting: The Mosasaurus. It is out there and it is in no hurry.
quests.gated: Not yet.

quests.label: Raise the Basilosaurus
quests.give: Fourth. Longest thing in the old water and the quietest. You will feel it before the line does.
quests.done: Four. I have started telling people about you, which is not a thing I do.
quests.waiting: The Basilosaurus. Long, slow, and worth the wait.
quests.gated: Not yet.

quests.label: Raise the Shastasaurus
quests.give: Fifth. The biggest of them that is not the last one, and the one I got closest to. Thirty seconds I held it. Then the water handed it back.
quests.done: Five. Five of six. There is one left and we both know which, and I have not been able to say its name out loud in years.
quests.waiting: The Shastasaurus. The one I nearly had. Go and finish what I could not.
quests.gated: Not yet.

quests.label: Raise the Megalodon
quests.give: The last one. It does not surface for anybody holding fewer than five, which is why no living captain has ever seen it and why I never will. It is yours. Go.
quests.done: All six. By one pair of hands, in one lifetime, and I watched it happen. ...Sit down. I need to tell you something, and you are not going to like where it starts.
quests.waiting: The Megalodon. It is waiting on you now, not the other way round.
quests.gated: Not yet. But it is going to be you.

residents.name: Nell Pollack

residents.name: Hattie Ling
residents.line: Long way out, better rate. That is the only reason anybody finds me.

residents.name: Sim Dory
residents.line: Dark water pays. Hold out, coin in, and mind how you go back up.

residents.name: Bess Skate
residents.line: Furthest scale on the chart. Whatever you have got, I will take it.

note.title: A chart scrap, weighted with a stone
note.body: Fish are worth more the further out you catch them. The lanes price by how far you hauled it, not by what it is, so a common thing from the deep can beat a rare thing from the shallows.

note.title: A note nailed to the post
note.body: The water goes in rings and each ring wants a better captain than the last. Open Waters asks Fishing 15, the Deep asks 30, the Abyss asks 50 and the Ancient Deep asks 75. Nothing out there is hidden. It is only far.

note.title: A page torn from a logbook
note.body: The shoals that shimmer are worth steering for. Three of them sit on this sea at any time, each one helping with something different, and they pick up and move about every ten minutes. Sail into one and it will tell you what it is doing for you.

note.title: A bottle, corked with wax
note.body: Watch the light. This sea runs a full turn from dawn back to dawn in about three quarters of an hour, and the mark up in the corner tells you where in it you are. Some out here only trade after dark.

note.title: A note in a tin, still dry
note.body: If the haul out here is wearing you down, it is the boat and not you. The Shipyard sells hull, and hull is the difference between a crossing you dread and one you do not think about. Stock rides at three hundred. It does not have to.

note.title: The last page of the Wreckwood log
note.body:
Day fifty one. We have eaten the bait and the cook has stopped pretending otherwise. He says the water here is older than the water at home and I have given up arguing.

Whoever finds this: the fishing is better nearer the shelf. Do not take our heading.

note.title: Scratched into the post itself
note.body:
We put in here to wait out the dark and the dark did not end. Counted eleven turns of it. On the ninth the youngest asked whether we had sailed past the morning and none of us had an answer worth giving her.

We are going on. The hold is empty and going back is further than going on.

note.title: A bundle of pages, tied with line
note.body:
The Farthing went down four lengths off this rock in water so still you could read by it. No squall. No reason. She simply stopped being a boat.

We pulled six of her crew out and left with them. If you are anchored here reading this, do not anchor here.

note.title: One line, cut deep
note.body:
We were nineteen days past the last rock anybody had named and we named this one anyway, because a thing with a name is a thing you can come back to.

We did not come back to it. Somebody should.
